sources.use: Section4.1 monopole Dirac spectrum; finite q=1 angular labels and degeneracies.
AdS2 Dirac canonical operator and invariant normalizable reference domain, Eqs21--25 and SecIII.C--D.

scope: A source-only sensitivity test on prescribed sharp-join geometries; no solved collar, shell material, formation, stability, or physical support is inferred.
q=1 is not the large-q MMP regime. Changing rho changes physical redshift, proper/optical length and the AdS reference with the endpoint lapse held one.
Both actual Weyl responses and all m=-N..N for N2/N4 are retained; these finite cutoffs do not complete the angular sum.
The reflected spin/gauge endpoint identification is a declared matching branch, not a derived physical junction.
Probe profiles are fixed fractions of sigma_cut: their proper support and geometric weights change with rho. All such data are retained.
Each phase compares the connected environment with its same-local-geometry invariant AdS reference. This is not a phase-pi-minus-zero result.
The unchanged constant-radius core has G_kk=0. A nonzero completed quantum source would require geometry response, not support the unchanged cylinder.
New numerical sources are still finite dissipative DG approximations. Observed mesh, angular-cut and ODE changes are not certified continuum or tail bounds.
This increment integrates only the finite x window [1e-6,48], equivalently the recorded kappa window. It does not integrate the saved three-node pilot.
N2/N4 sums each complete their own finite angular multiplets, with both actual Weyl responses; no full angular completion or arbitrary degeneracy scaling.
The observed quadrature envelope, matched-order mesh difference, N4-minus-N2 change and selected outer J11-minus-J9 change are distinct diagnostics.
The two low-frequency samples and high-frequency x96 sample are actual source evaluations, not assumed extrapolations or certified omitted-integral bounds.
No tail-cache hook is added to the frozen solver. Existing radial caches are reused; no global monkeypatching or historical source changes occur.
